Hi Aditya 

Thanks for the demo today. Good conversation. Quick recap on what we need to validate from Redwood to proceed with procurement: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 300ms at p95 for single-turn chat responses. Our UI requires the first token to appear within that window to keep the typing indicator tight.
- Streaming: we plan to surface streaming completions in the patient-facing chat. Prefer SSE or WebSocket with small chunk cadence  target ~100ms between chunks or ~2050 tokens per chunk depending on model output.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline expected concurrency 50 simultaneous active sessions, burst to 200 for peak events. Average requests ~250 RPS across endpoints during business hours.
- Latency SLOs for tail: p99 should be <= 900ms for first token, otherwise we plan to fallback to a non-streaming fast path.

Attached is a rough requirements sheet (acme-ttft-requirements.xlsx) with traffic patterns. Can you confirm whether your hosted API or Dedicated tier can meet these numbers and what config you’d recommend (batching, KV cache, quantization)?

Also, who should be our technical contact for an on-call test next week?

Best,
Samir
Senior Product Manager
Acme Health

Samir 

Great meeting, thanks for the detailed sheet. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps: 

- Can meet TTFT p95 <= 300ms on Hosted for moderate load (<=100 concurrent) using streaming-optimized model variants and prefix caching. For sustained concurrency of 50 with bursts to 200, we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) to keep consistent latency.
- Streaming: Redwood supports SSE and WebSocket. Typical chunk cadence we configure is 80150ms depending on model and tokenization  we’ll tune to your UI. Our suggestion is target ~100ms cadence with chunk sizes of 1664 tokens (model dependent); we can provide a reference config.
- Throughput/concurrency: with Dedicated and autoscale policy set to keep at least N=4 inference workers per model shard, we can sustain your 250 RPS baseline with headroom for bursts. Exact numbers depend on model choice and quantization.
- Failover: we can set automatic fallback to a smaller, faster variant if TTFT begins to slip beyond p95 threshold.

Next steps: 
1) Quick tech sync: Wed 22 May 10:00 PT  bring one of your backend engineers for a short connectivity/streaming test (SSE).
2) Redwood will run a 1-hour load test in staging (we’ll simulate 50200 concurrency and measure TTFT at p50/p95/p99).
3) Post-test, we’ll share a short report and a recommended Dedicated sizing + suggested batching/cache configs.

I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Dev (solutions engineer) to coordinate the test.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Load test details: Redwood will run a 1-hour staged test with the following probes:
